evidence: Disassembly 0x38338-0x38380: lhz 0x40b7ba >= lhz 0x4087a8, or lha 0x40a7c0 (cold_start_phase) = 3, then lhz 0x3fe9a2 (fault_detected_bits_368_to_383) bit 0 clear gives li r3,1, else li r3,0. Reached only through the 4-entry function pointer table at ROM 0x57730 (0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c): cm848_updateAlternatorFieldRegulatorState (0x376dc) builds 0x57730 with lis/addi (0x37714-0x37718), loads entry [state] with lwzx (0x37720), calls it indirectly and stores the returned r3 as the next state. A scan of every 4-byte word of ROM 0x0-0x6ffff and flash 2 finds no b / bl / bc to any handler and no other pointer to them, which is why Ghidra left them as LAB_ code. plate_comment: Setpoint stage of the actuator E control loop: takes the wastegate duty request (wastegate_duty_controller_state.request_half_duty_counts, 12800 = 100 percent), replaces it with actuator_e_setpoint_override when bit 0 of actuator_e_override_flags_cal is set, caps it at actuator_e_setpoint_upper_limit (12800) and, while bit 0x4000 of governor_status_flags is set, clamps it to the margin actuator_e_end_margin (1856) from both ends; the result is actuator_e_setpoint_working (10896 in the dump). Called by cm848_updateActuatorESetpointAndMode. (was cm848_calculateSpeedControlLimit)

The wastegate solenoid reads the request directly (cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty: 2 x request) and nothing writes the request back. The request is only the SETPOINT of a separate closed loop whose feedback is ADC sensor channel 101 (0x65) and whose only outputs are a PWM duty to output channel actuator_output_channel_e_cal (0 = unassigned in this calibration) and logical output 71 (protection_event_output_line_cal word [71] = 0 in the RAM dump = no output line), see the loop note below. plate_comment: Final scaling and limiting of the actuator E drive command: multiplies governor_fuel_output_a_working by boost_fuel_scale_cal / fuel_timing_error_scale (224 / 192 in the dump: 8905 -> 10389), derives the upper and lower limits from governor_rpm_limit_working and the limit calibrations, and stores the limited signed command in actuator_e_drive_command. text: ACTUATOR E LOOP (answer to the uncertain item 0x2ca14). The chain cm848_initProtectionModeDefaults -> cm848_processSpeedControlModeLogic / cm848_calculateSpeedControlFiltered / cm848_processFuelControlOutput (0x2c9bc-0x2dc00) is neither an engine speed governor, nor fuel control, nor conditioning of the wastegate duty. It is a separate closed loop: SETPOINT = wastegate_duty_controller_state.request_half_duty_counts (same 12800 = 100 percent scale; the wastegate solenoid reads the request directly, so the wastegate reading of the struct is final and does not depend on this chain); FEEDBACK = governor_speed_tracking, which cm848_calculateDiagnosticStatusBits takes from ADC sensor channel 101 (0x65: cm848_protection_init_configBundle passes protection_channel_filtered_output as the filtered value, protection_derate_fallback_speed as the default value 0x2400 and protection_fault_condition_value as the fault state; the same value / default / fault triple as the barometric channel); OUTPUT = signed command -> direction on logical output 71 + PWM duty x 2 on output channel actuator_output_channel_e_cal (output function 43 'actuator e', period j1939_governor_output_param_cal = 2857 microseconds). In this truck's calibration both are unassigned (channel 0, protection_event_output_line_cal word [71] = 0), while governor_fuel_b_mode_flag = 1 keeps the loop running (dump: setpoint 10896, feedback 1991, command 10389, duty 20778, actuator_e_duty_command 0). Likely physical role (inference): the position servo of an optional electric boost actuator whose position command is the turbo controller's request; supporting facts: sign + magnitude + dead band + zero-duty pass on reversal (H-bridge style drive), a fixed-output control mode 4 selected while fault_threshold_condition_flag (set by the start-up stage cm848_evaluateLoadProtectionFuelLowStage with its 60-pass warm-up timer) is on, a tracking monitor (engine_protection_speedTracking_calc: ramped setpoint minus feedback against a threshold, together with the signed drive command) and a motion monitor (governor_rpm_monitor_calc: |command| x fuel_timing_error_scale against the change of the channel 101 value). The identity of sensor channel 101 and of actuator E is open.

DOMAIN CONFLICT (read first): the applied 2026-06-27 engine-load-protection re-domain (plate of cm848_processLoadProtectionStatus, commit 7c997eb, ~18 functions in 0x2e17c-0x2f6a0 plus the ENGINE_LOAD_PROTECTION_STATE enum) says the monitored quantity is engine_load_percent EMA-filtered into protection_ema_output. The code does not do that: cm848_updateLoadProtectionEmaOutput low-pass filters protection_channel_filtered_output (0x40bdb6), which cm848_protection_init_configBundle / update_configBundle pass as the value output of ADC sensor channel 101 (0x65, same argument layout as the barometric call: index, fault bits 0x2aa / 0x2ab, value / default / fault-state pointers; the CSV comment of 0x40bdb6 also says it mirrors sensor_channel_filtered_output[0x65]). xref_addr.py on engine_load_percent (0x40af24) lists 9 functions, none of them in 0x2e17c-0x2f6a0 (diag_boostLoad_overtemp_monitor, cm848_calibration_group21_load, the PCI / OBD / SCI readers, cm848_detectVehicleSpeedSensorSignalLoss, cm848_monitorWastegateBoostPressure); cm848_processLoadProtectionStatus only names it in its plate text. The old name of 0x40af24 was protection_channel_load_raw, the likely source of the mix-up. cm848_evaluateLoadProtectionSteadyStage / ...FuelLowStage compare |12800 - channel 101 value| with 1856, the same margin the actuator E setpoint clamp uses. So the cm848_evaluateLoadProtection* / cm848_calculateLoadProtection* / cm848_updateLoadProtection* functions and the protection_* words (confirm counters, ema output, load filtered, derate target, governor_status_flags 0x4000 / 0x8000) read like the start-up learn and supervision stages of the actuator E loop, not a load-derate governor. Not renamed here: sensor channel 101's physical identity is open and the cluster is large; review it before more names are built on the load-protection reading.

Chain names left unchanged (not settled): cm848_checkSpeedZeroCondition (0x2caa0), cm848_calculateSpeedControlRampUp / RampDown (0x2cbe8 / 0x2cc90), cm848_updateSpeedControlOutputs (0x2cd38), cm848_selectSpeedControlGains (0x2cdb4: only picks the high / low gain set by comparing the setpoint with governor_gain_select_fuel_threshold_cal), mpc555_initFuelControlModeVariables, cm848_updateSpeedControlCounter1/2 and ...Filter1/2; the remaining governor_* / throttle_* / fuel_control_* words of this chain (governor_speed_*, governor_fuel_output_*, governor_fuel_integral_b, throttle_speed_rate_*, governor_output_prev_*, governor_rpm_monitored) are in the same domain and should be renamed together in one pass. throttle_speed_rate_cal (0x40b06a) is a RAM flag written by cm848_evaluateLoadProtectionOverspeedStage, so the _cal suffix is wrong. governor_fuel_b_mode_flag (0x40776e) is NOT specific to this loop (9 readers, including phase_group_b_computeGovernorFuelDemandOutput), so it keeps its name.
